source_review: Literal program/type/selector/C-body comparison; not a formal Haskell translation

canonical_regions.text:
, nonceHash = ih &&& oh
            >>> match (ih &&& take (zero word8) >>> ctx8Add1)
                (ih &&& take (copair (take (copair (scribe (toWord8 0x02)) (scribe (toWord8 0x03))) &&& ih) ((unit >>> scribe (toWord8 0x01)) &&& iden))
                 >>> (oh &&& ioh >>> ctx8Add1) &&& iih >>> ctx8Add32)
type Conf a = Either Point a

oh :: (Core term, TyC x, TyC b) => term (x, b) x
oh = take iden

ih :: (Core term, TyC a, TyC x) => term (a, x) x
ih = drop iden

ooh :: (Core term, TyC x, TyC b, TyC c) => term ((x, b), c) x
ooh = take oh

oih :: (Core term, TyC a, TyC x, TyC c) => term ((a, x), c) x
oih = take ih

ioh :: (Core term, TyC a, TyC x, TyC c) => term (a, (x, c)) x
ioh = drop oh

iih :: (Core term, TyC a, TyC b, TyC x) => term (a, (b, x)) x
iih = drop ih

observations: Explicit adds 0x01 then all 32 payload bytes; C skips its one sum-padding bit.
Confidential adds 0x02 or 0x03 according to parity, then all 32 payload bytes.
Payload is an arbitrary Word256; no field or on-curve restriction is added.
Literal sequence retained: ctx8Add1 for the prefix, ctx8Addn vector32 for the payload.
Body equality and function entry are preparation, not complete C-jet execution.
